newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil slips as premium drop erases IPE gains.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil slips as premium drop erases IPE gains.

text.p: NWE heating oil premiums weakened on Tuesday, erasing modest gains on IPE futures, but diesel was steady in a standoff over early February supply, traders said.
The Feb IPE contract closed up 75 cents at $200.50 a tonne.

Traders said heating oil barge premiums slipped about $1 with refinery product concluded between Feb IPE +$3/4 a tonne for first half February. Prompt refinery material was heard concluded at Feb IPE +$4.
Storage barges were talked at a 50 cent discount to refinery material.
Cargoes were quiet with end-users looking relaxed and under no pressure to buy. Buying into Germany was muted on the back of high stocks and continued problems over frozen waterways.
Diesel premiums held steady at Feb IPE gas oil +$15/18, the wide range reflecting a sharp difference between buyers and sellers over the prospects for early month supply.
German heating oil cargoes were heard bid at Feb IPE +$7 with offers pegged at +$8/9, but nothing was thought done.
Russian material was showing a premium to Feb IPE of +$3/3.50 cif NWE.
